name: Cliff Top Club Restaurant
signature_dish: vegetable pakoras with chai at altitude
why_it_matters: Auli's longest-running ski resort restaurant — buffet breakfast, à-la-carte lunch, set dinner. The kitchen openly admits ingredients are constrained by the road from Joshimath, which is why simple dishes (pakoras, dal-chawal) outperform the Chinese section.
insider_tip: Stay-guests get full board built into the tariff; walk-ins should call ahead — they sometimes refuse outside diners during peak ski season because the kitchen is sized for in-house occupancy.
signature_address: Cliff Top Club, Auli Road, Auli, Chamoli 246443

name: GMVN Tourist Rest House Restaurant
why_it_matters: The state-run Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam canteen — vegetarian and non-vegetarian thali, in-house bar, government tariff. The cheapest hot meal in Auli and the only option that takes outside walk-ins reliably.
insider_tip: Eat in the dining hall, not in your room — the kitchen is at the far end of the complex and food cools fast on the walk back. Open to non-residents but they'll ask you to wait until in-house guests are served.
signature_address: GMVN Tourist Complex, near ITBP, Auli, Joshimath, Chamoli 246443

name: Alpenrose at The Tattva
signature_dish: Garhwali pahadi thali with mandua roti
why_it_matters: The closest thing to fine-dining on the Joshimath-Auli stretch — chandelier room facing the Great Himalaya wall, paired with The Bourbon Club lounge for whisky and cocktails. Multi-cuisine menu spans pahadi to Lebanese.
insider_tip: Sit at the window-side table after sundown — Nanda Devi catches the last light around 5:30pm in winter. The pahadi section of the menu is more honest than the Lebanese — order accordingly.
signature_address: Shri Badrinath Dham Road, Near Tapovan Taxi Stand, Upper Bazar, Joshimath 246443

name: Oryza at Casa Himalaya
why_it_matters: One of the few Auli kitchens that takes the local Garhwali repertoire seriously — kafuli (spinach-fenugreek), chaunsa (black soyabean dal), laal bhaat (red rice). Floor-to-ceiling French doors face the Himalaya; cedar-wood patio for fair weather.
insider_tip: Order from the local section, not the international one — the kitchen sources organic ingredients from farms below Joshimath specifically for the Garhwali dishes. Skip the Chinese.

name: The Ski Story Cafe
signature_dish: hot chocolate after a ski run
why_it_matters: Marketed as the first standalone cafe in Auli — small, casual room attached to Casa Himalaya. Hot chocolate, coffee, fried snacks; the kind of place to sit between ski runs without committing to a hotel meal.
insider_tip: Open to non-residents; arrive mid-afternoon (2-4pm) when ski instructors stop in for chai — that's when the kitchen has the most snacks ready.

name: Auli Meadows Restaurant
signature_dish: Garhwali set meal with seasonal greens
why_it_matters: Camp-resort kitchen on the Auli Road with an in-house multi-cuisine restaurant — meals included for camping guests, à-la-carte for walk-ins. Bonfire-side dinners served in winter when the snow allows.
insider_tip: Day visitors can book a meal in advance via the resort's number — they don't actively cater walk-ins but will accommodate if you call from Joshimath before driving up.
signature_address: Auli Road, Auli Laga Joshimath, Chamoli 246443

name: Auli-D Food Plaza
why_it_matters: Indian-Chinese-continental restaurant on NH-58 in Joshimath, near the Auli ropeway base station — the practical lunch stop before or after the cable-car ride up. Veg, non-veg and Jain options all on one menu.
insider_tip: Open 9am-11pm; if you've taken the ropeway down at sunset and missed your hotel dinner window, this is the closest sit-down option to the Joshimath cable-car terminus.
signature_address: NH-58, Near Punjab National Bank, Joshimath, Chamoli 246443
